abstract:
Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline.
BioLM-Score integrates frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings into a residue-atom distance-likelihood framework via gated graph convolutions. We evaluate geometry-only, jointly trained, and two-stage fine-tuned variants, using the jointly trained variant for the primary controlled comparisons. All three DEKOIS 2.0 screening endpoints improve over the matched geometric baseline with target-level paired support, but affinity scoring and ranking do not improve uniformly. Under a time-split protocol, scoring is significantly lower and ranking is also lower than the geometric baseline, while screening gains persist. On BDB2020+, the difference in affinity correlation between BioLM-Score and GenScore narrows after LP-PDBBind-compatible retraining. Shuffling protein embeddings at inference reduces the screening advantage. However, retrained shuffle controls recover much of the performance, so correct alignment is not established as necessary. BioLM-Score strengthens geometric scoring on screening tasks without retraining the language models.
Code, dataset-split identifiers, preprocessing and evaluation scripts, and language-model embedding-generation utilities are available at https://github.com/SZU-ADDG/BioLM-Score. An archival code snapshot and pretrained model weights are available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.21878818.
Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
